newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FOCUS - Bull run pushes East European bourses higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bull run pushes East European bourses higher.

text.p: A strong bull run brought a flying start for most East European stocks in the first week of trading this year with Warsaw hitting record highs and prices soaring in Budapest and Prague.
Bratislava shifted to higher gear and shares in Ljubliana, Zagreb and Bucharest were on the rise. Tirana had no trades and Bulgaria stock trading remained suspended.
WARSAW
Polish shares soared this week, setting two consecutive 33-month highs on Wednesday and Thursday in heavy turnovers and analysts expected them to extend gains thanks to foreign institutional buying.

"We've really got the impetus and it's a good sign that the demand is generated by foreign funds, which we can tell from the turnover figure and demand on large caps," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Some analysts said the strong resistance level for the WIG index would be 16,000 points, but others saw the index surging to 18,000 points in the next two months.
But they said a lot would depend on the companies' December and preliminary 1996 earnings reports due next week.
BUDAPEST
The Budapest Stock Exchange began the year in an euphoric mood with the BUX index steadily climbing from last December's rally.

The BUX hit the 14th successive record high in a row on Thursday, closing at 4,724.59 points, up 161.76. The BUX has more than tripled since the beginning of 1996 and rose 14 percent from December 31.

Traders said the bull run was driven by fresh interest of foreign and domestic investors on a worldwide rising trend on stock markets. Good Hungarian macroeconomic figures and corporate results also underpinned investors sentiment that Hungarian shares were undervalued.
The pace of the rally took traders by surprise. Even though a downwards correction may come any time, they said Hungarian stocks were likely to extend their gains substantially in 1997.
PRAGUE

Czech shares took off with gains this year and analysts say foreign investors may be diverting their attention to the relatively undervalued PX50 after realising strong gains last year in Warsaw and Budapest.
"We cannot expect the same strong interest in Poland and Hungary so the investors have decided to put money into the Czech Republic," said Miroslav Nosal of Patria Finance.

Last year the PX50 index rose by just 27 percent compared with well over 100 percent in Budapest and nearly 90 percent in Warsaw. In the week to Thursday, the PX50 rose 2.9 percent to 555.5 powered by strong performances from major issues.
BRATISLAVA
Trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange opened listless this week, but brokers said they expected activity to pick up, boosted mainly by foreign investors.
The 12-share SAX index closed at 179.20 points on Thursday, up 1.15 from Tuesday open at 178.05.
Brokers also said demand for blue chips and reluctance to sell at the currently prices may underpin the upward trend.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares this week rose 7.31 percent. The ten-share SBI index rose 86.6 points to 1,271.8. Total turnover was 746.9 million tolars ($5.2 million).
Health resort Terme Catez operator was the biggest gainer, jumping 20.98 percent, while warehouse BTC was the leading decliner, falling 33.9 percent.
BUCHAREST

Most Bucharest bourse shares drifted higher this week, with turnover climbing to 70 million lei on Tuesday before sinking to a quarter of that level on Thursday amid thin trading interest, brokers said.
Fertiliser-maker Azomures SA stayed in the limelight, gaining 1,200 lei on Thursday to close at 14,300.
Two unofficial indices - the VAB, computed by Vanguard SA and Bucharest Investment Group 's BIG -- rose by 2.9 percent and 2.72 percent from the previous session.
ZAGREB

Croatian stocks forged ahead this week, with fully listed drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka losing pace on Thursday, and traders expected a slight stagnation before prices firm up again in the near future.

All eyes are set on the credit rating Croatia is expected to get next week, when three leading rating agencies are to announce their assessment. It is widely expected to be solid and should help prop up prices of all liquid stocks.
TIRANA
Albania's fledgling Tirana Stock Exchange started the year with two eventless sessions on Monday and Thursday.
"Everybody was in a selling mood because they seemed to need liquidity but no deals were struck," a broker said.
The eight-month-old exchange trades in 364-day government treasury bills, bonds and privatisation vouchers.
